decisions.reason: Glass-silicon wafers with through contacts build on the firm's core structuring competence, carry substantial process investment, and fit its announced direction toward multifunctional packaging wafers, so dropping them would write off sunk R&D.
Carrier wafers for thin-wafer handling were publicly announced, fit the stated strategy of reusable carriers, and need little extra cost to keep in the range.

The Cu-interposer was launched visibly at SEMICON Europa with its own web page and embodies costly technology development, so management will attribute slow uptake to temporary market and pandemic conditions rather than withdraw it.
The Wafer Universe brand is a public commitment selling standard products close to the core business at low marginal cost, so there is little reason to abandon it.

Glass-based circuit boards are distant from the core business and were only mentioned briefly, so they are the most likely candidate for withdrawal, but the EU-funded development effort and the glass-substrate packaging trend still give management a reason to persist.
